The Guardian (Heather Stewart) — published 2026-09-29 (date confirmed from the URL path /2026/sep/29/ and returned metadata; no time confirmed). Search highlights (WebFetch refused for theguardian.com).
"Will pensioners be poorer as a result of Burnham scrapping the triple lock?"
Strapline: Original triple lock was designed to lift pensioners out of poverty but OBR says it contributes to unsustainability of public finances.
From 2030, under what Labour is calling an "adjusted triple lock", the pension will still rise either in line with prices, or 2.5% each year, whichever is higher - but it won't rise in line with earnings unless its value has fallen behind. In that case, it will be adjusted so that it keeps pace.
IFS: the cost of providing the state pension in 2026/27 will be £154bn, making it the most costly benefit in the UK.
The new policy removes what the Resolution Foundation has called the "ratchet" effect.
Labour says pensions have risen significantly relative to average earnings since the policy was introduced; stresses that under the new approach it will still rise every year and won't fall behind average earnings over time. By not introducing it until after the next general election, they argue the public will be given a say.
OBR: has pointed to the triple lock as one factor contributing to the unsustainability of the public finances; predicted about 9% of GDP would have been spent on state pensions by 2075/76 if the triple lock had remained, up from 5% currently.
